findings.title: Auto-start executes scripts from an untrusted working directory
findings.description:
**File:** [`apps/cli/src/agent-runtime.ts`](https://github.com/OxFrancesco/BeeGreat/blob/main/apps/cli/src/agent-runtime.ts#L62-L159) (lines 62, 63, 68, 85, 86, 87, 142, 143, 156, 157, 159)
**Project:** BeeGreat
**Severity:** HIGH  •  **Confidence:** high  •  **Slug:** `rce`

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `oddofrancesco000@gmail.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

findBeeProjectRoot() searches process.cwd() before the CLI installation directory. It accepts a directory when its package.json names it 'beegreat' and packages/agent/package.json exists, then runs 'bun run agent' there with the user's environment and permissions. An attacker can distribute a checkout containing these files and a malicious agent script. If the user invokes the installed Bee CLI from that checkout with no BEE_PROJECT_ROOT override, default auto-start enabled, and the local agent unavailable, Bee executes the attacker's script without a trust decision. The README recommends setting BEE_PROJECT_ROOT for global launchers, but the code does not enforce that requirement.

## Recommendation

Resolve automatic startup from the trusted CLI installation or an explicitly configured installation path. Remove implicit execution from cwd-discovered repositories, or require explicit trust before running their scripts.

## Finding

canonicalWeb3Reply renders both the transaction text and confirmation prompt through helpers that replace every EVM address with generic wording such as 'the selected address'. The backend's prepareSendTokensForUser includes the actual recipient in its canonical summary, but that recipient is removed before CLI approval. The subsequent confirmation submits the unsanitized canonical summary and executes the actual recipient stored in the action. An attacker who influences the recipient through external content or model tool arguments can therefore make a substituted destination indistinguishable in the trusted confirmation display. Backend summary equality does not restore the missing user-visible destination.

## Recommendation

Display transaction-critical fields, including the actual recipient, chain, token, and amount, from the canonical action. Exempt these fields from identifier scrubbing and bind approval to the details presented.

**Suggested assignee:** `oddofrancesco000@gmail.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

Input submitted while busy is stored as an unbound string. When a reply requires confirmation, showFollowUp suppresses the confirmation panel if the queue is nonempty, and the finally block immediately submits the queued text. session.ts interprets a queued 'yes' as authorization for the newly populated pendingWeb3 action and calls confirm_web3. Consequently, text entered before the transaction was presented can authorize a funds transfer. An attacker-influenced agent response can exploit this timing when a user has queued an affirmative response. Backend ownership, expiry, and summary checks accept the request because it carries the victim's credentials and canonical action summary.

## Recommendation

Pause queue processing whenever a confirmation appears. Require a fresh decision bound to the displayed action ID, and prevent previously queued chat text from becoming transaction authorization.

findings.title: Performance transactions bypass credential redaction
findings.description:
**File:** [`apps/codex-adapter/sentry.server.config.ts`](https://github.com/OxFrancesco/BeeGreat/blob/main/apps/codex-adapter/sentry.server.config.ts#L14-L18) (lines 14, 15, 18)
**Project:** BeeGreat
**Severity:** HIGH  •  **Confidence:** high  •  **Slug:** `secret-in-log`

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `oddofrancesco000@gmail.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

Tracing is enabled at a 20% production sampling rate, but sanitizeSentryEvent is registered only as beforeSend. Sentry invokes that hook for error events, not transaction events. The inspected SDK's HTTP instrumentation stores incoming request headers in normalizedRequest, and its default RequestData integration copies those headers into transaction.request.headers. sendDefaultPii: false removes IP-related headers but does not remove authorization or x-flue-codex-adapter-secret from this event field. Authenticated POST /api/codex/responses requests carry both the ChatGPT bearer token and the shared adapter secret, so sampled transactions transmit these credentials to Sentry. Someone with access to the resulting telemetry could reuse the bearer token and adapter secret. No beforeSendTransaction hook or application event processor closes this gap.

## Recommendation

Register sanitizeSentryEvent as beforeSendTransaction as well. Disable request-header collection through RequestData integration options if it is unnecessary, and explicitly sanitize span attributes. If tracing has been enabled in production, investigate existing telemetry and rotate exposed credentials.

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `oddofrancesco000@gmail.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

The message loop authenticates message.sender.id but never checks whether space.type is 'dm'. The installed Spectrum iMessage provider delivers group messages and preserves the originating group as space. For linked senders, the bridge retrieves their private conversation context and sends progress and account-derived replies into that group. For unknown senders, welcomeUnknownSender sends the address-link bearer token into the group. Another participant can redeem that token using their own Clerk account: imessageAuth.completeLink and imessage.completeLinkSession treat possession of the token as proof of address ownership. This lets a group participant link someone else's address to their account and receive future conversation content synchronized under that account.

## Recommendation

Require a verified direct-message space before resolving identities, issuing links, or processing private account requests. Send linking tokens only through a DM explicitly opened for the sender's verified address. If group support is intended, give it separate authorization and conversation state.

findings.description:
**File:** [`packages/agent/src/app.ts`](https://github.com/OxFrancesco/BeeGreat/blob/main/packages/agent/src/app.ts#L19-L74) (lines 19, 20, 21, 72, 73, 74)

**Suggested assignee:** `oddofrancesco000@gmail.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

These mounts always expose GitHub, Linear, and Notion webhook handlers, and authGate explicitly exempts their webhook paths. Each channel obtains its signing key from shared/beennectors/channel.ts, where channelSecret substitutes the public value `unconfigured-${name.toLowerCase()}` when configuration is absent. Flue accepts that value as a valid HMAC key. An unauthenticated attacker can therefore sign fabricated deliveries when the corresponding secret is missing. Supplying a connected victim's external account or workspace ID makes claimDelivery resolve the victim, and an active subscription allows dispatchBee to inject attacker-controlled signals into that victim's agent. Signature checks, subscription checks, and delivery deduplication do not establish authenticity when the signing key is predictable.

## Recommendation

Remove deterministic signing-key fallbacks. Disable each webhook route or return a configuration error until its real provider secret is available. Require secrets for enabled channels during deployment validation.

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `oddofrancesco000@gmail.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

The webhookSecret uses channelSecret(), which returns the public constant 'unconfigured-github_webhook_secret' when configuration is absent or blank. The Flue adapter accepts valid HMAC signatures made with that constant, and /channels/github/webhook explicitly bypasses Clerk and bridge authentication. An unauthenticated attacker who knows a connected user's public GitHub account ID can supply it as payload.sender.id and forge an allowed event with arbitrary comment content and a fresh delivery ID. Convex maps the supplied actor to the connected user; its subscription check only requires that victim to have an active subscription. The worker then dispatches attacker-controlled content into that user's Bee agent. Exploitation requires the deployment to lack a real GitHub webhook secret.

## Recommendation

Remove the deterministic fallback. Reject webhook requests or omit channel registration when the real secret is unavailable. Keep local build support separate from production webhook authentication.

findings.title: Executable Astro content bypasses the guarded workspace restrictions
findings.description:
**File:** [`packages/agent/src/shared/bee-sites/astro-creator.ts`](https://github.com/OxFrancesco/BeeGreat/blob/main/packages/agent/src/shared/bee-sites/astro-creator.ts#L21-L527) (lines 21, 253, 254, 481, 518, 522, 525, 527)
**Project:** BeeGreat
**Severity:** HIGH  •  **Confidence:** high  •  **Slug:** `rce`

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `oddofrancesco000@gmail.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

write_site_file validates the filename and content length but accepts arbitrary Astro frontmatter and expressions. check_site, preview_site, and publish_site subsequently execute astro build, which runs that code with Node filesystem and process capabilities. An attacker-controlled component copied into a site can therefore execute commands and modify files outside the selected workspace, including other sites belonging to the same user. bee.ts reuses one sandbox per user, and workspace preparation trusts an existing package.json, allowing modifications to persist across subsequent tasks while that sandbox remains alive. The filename allowlist and public worker's no-script CSP do not restrict build-time execution. The demonstrated scope is the site sandbox, not a Cloudflare host escape or access to worker secrets.

## Recommendation

Treat Astro source as executable untrusted code. Build each revision in an isolated disposable environment with a read-only starter, access only to that revision's files, restricted network access, and enforced resource limits. If executable templates are unnecessary, accept a declarative content format rendered by trusted templates.

findings.title: Delayed purchase webhook can override newer inactive subscription state
findings.description:
**File:** [`packages/backend/convex/subscriptions.ts`](https://github.com/OxFrancesco/BeeGreat/blob/main/packages/backend/convex/subscriptions.ts#L55-L476) (lines 55, 160, 188, 189, 442, 451, 452, 455, 465, 471, 476)

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `oddofrancesco000@gmail.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

An inactive REST reconciliation stores its observation timestamp in subscriptionStatusChecks but only updates entitlement rows that already exist. If no entitlement row exists, a subsequently delivered older INITIAL_PURCHASE or RENEWAL webhook bypasses the stale-event check because applyRevenueCatEvent compares timestamps only against an existing entitlement row. It never consults subscriptionStatusChecks. For example, RevenueCat can report a purchase as refunded before its original purchase webhook reaches this backend; that delayed webhook then inserts an active entitlement using the original future expiration. subscriptionStatus ignores the newer check's inactive flag, and the webhook refreshes the cache timestamp. On deployments with REQUIRE_SUBSCRIPTION=true, the affected subscriber can regain paid chat and voice access until another reconciliation or revocation corrects the state. subscriptionReconciliation.ts reuses this cached result for up to 60 seconds.

## Recommendation

Consult the latest REST observation timestamp when applying webhook grants, including when no entitlement row exists. Reject events superseded by an authoritative snapshot, or require reconciliation before granting access. Preserve the inactive ordering record and cover delayed purchase events after an initial inactive snapshot.

findings.title: Unsolicited NFT transfers can halt wallet automation
findings.description:
**File:** [`packages/sugar/src/alm/engine.ts`](https://github.com/OxFrancesco/BeeGreat/blob/main/packages/sugar/src/alm/engine.ts#L131-L501) (lines 131, 138, 418, 498, 499, 500, 501)

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `oddofrancesco000@gmail.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

The engine identifies the replacement NFT by comparing wallet-owned positions before and after the rebalance and requiring exactly one new ID. An attacker can transfer a funded NFT from the same pool to the managed wallet after previousIds is captured and before the final lookup. Receiving this transfer requires no victim authorization. Both the legitimate replacement and the donated NFT become candidates, causing the engine to throw before staking or completing the cycle. The persisted active cycle then blocks all subsequent ALM cycles for that wallet and chain until manual recovery, even across restarts. Configuring an explicit positionId does not prevent this because replacement discovery still examines all new wallet-owned NFTs.

## Recommendation

Derive the replacement NFT ID from the confirmed deposit transaction's NFPM mint event, validate its owner, pool, and range, and persist that ID. Do not infer transaction provenance from changes in wallet inventory.

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `oddofrancesco000@gmail.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

The action reads a pending session without atomically claiming it before exchanging the authorization code. Two callbacks can therefore exchange the same single-use code concurrently. If the second exchange fails after the first consumes the code but before the first stores its credentials, the second callback calls failSession and changes the session to failed. The successful callback then reaches beennectors.completeAuthorization, which rejects non-pending sessions. A duplicate callback can thus make a valid connection fail and discard the issued credentials.

## Recommendation

Atomically claim the pending session before exchanging its code. Associate completion and failure with that claim, and make duplicate callbacks observe the existing operation instead of starting another exchange.

resolveForAgent claims a refresh lease, then awaits refreshCredentials without a timeout or lease renewal. chatgptAuth.ts allows another caller to replace that lease after 30 seconds, while chatgptOpenAi.ts performs an unbounded fetch. If the first request remains pending beyond that period, a second caller can submit the same refresh token. The first successful response is then discarded because finishRefresh rejects its superseded lease. Keep exclusive ownership throughout refresh and persistence. Renew the lease while work is active, impose a bounded request lifetime, and handle uncertain upstream completion without immediately replaying the old refresh token.

The shared CLI/iMessage confirmation displays this summary, and approving a smart-wallet action schedules server signing without another wallet review. A mistaken generated duration can therefore lock funds until an undisclosed expiry. The refresh bounds preserve the stored duration but do not make it visible to the user.

## Recommendation

Render veNFT confirmation terms from plan.ve_nft, including the normalized token amount, token symbol, lock duration, and inability to withdraw before expiry. Use those terms consistently in every confirmation channel.

## Finding

The notifier awaits child.exited without a timeout and reads piped stderr only after exit. A stalled buddytg process can therefore prevent the notifier from returning; sufficiently large stderr output can also block the child before it exits. The engine awaits notifications within runPass while holding the ALM state lock, so a notification failure can stop subsequent position processing and prevent other processes from acquiring the lock. Enforce a notification deadline, terminate and reap the child on timeout, and drain stderr concurrently while retaining only bounded diagnostic output. Log the failure and return so the engine can release its lock and continue.

## Finding

## Finding

A basic-pool holder can have both staked LP tokens and unstaked LP tokens with accrued fees. The basic Pool.claimFees implementation in resources/aerodrome-contracts/contracts/Pool.sol pays the caller's accrued fees without requiring a gauge or checking their staked balance. findings.title: An invalidated analytics load can overwrite a newer report
findings.description:
**File:** [`packages/sugar/src/tui/analytics/load.ts`](https://github.com/OxFrancesco/BeeGreat/blob/main/packages/sugar/src/tui/analytics/load.ts#L175-L195) (lines 175, 176, 177, 178, 179, 194, 195)

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `oddofrancesco000@gmail.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

invalidateReport deletes the cache entry without cancelling its running load. The TUI worker invokes this operation on Ctrl+R, allowing a replacement load to overlap the previous one. If the replacement finishes first, the previous load subsequently fails the startedAt comparison and enters the else branch, replacing the newer cache entry with its own report and promise. It also unconditionally overwrites the disk snapshot. Subsequent screen visits or sessions can therefore display superseded analytics, including a partial report replacing a successful refresh. This is a non-security cache race established by source inspection.

## Recommendation

Associate each load with a unique entry or generation token. Update the shared cache and disk snapshot only when that load still owns the current entry. An invalidated or superseded load should return to its original caller without changing shared state.

During wallet creation or restoration, screens/wallet.tsx opens another PromptDialog for passphrase confirmation inside that callback. The dialog host in app.tsx renders topDialog.node without using the dialog's unique ID as a React key.
